# `/` — Reduce

Monadic operator. Hanzi: `总` (`總`)

`f/Y` inserts `f` between the items along the last axis, then evaluates that expression as usual, from the right. `-/1 2 3` is `1-2-3`, which is 2. An empty axis reduces to `f`'s identity.

```bpl
+/1 2 3            ⍝ 6
-/1 2 3            ⍝ 2
+/⍬                ⍝ 0
```

Reduction returns the accumulator. An unseeded one-item reduction returns that item. Unreduced axes supply the result frame.

A dfn that reduces several lanes, such as each row of a matrix, runs each stage on every lane at once, in a [batched call](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects). The result is the same as reducing each lane in turn.

```bpl
,/⊂2 3            ⍝ 2 3
,/,⊂2 3           ⍝ 2 3
+/⊂⊂3             ⍝ ⊂3
```

`S f/ Y` starts from seed `S` on the right. With `Y` holding `[a b c]`, it is `a f b f c f S`. Empty reductions return the seed. Each lane uses the whole seed. The seed can share a run with the reduction, as in `10-/1 2 3`. With a space, `10 -/1 2 3` is the strand `10 2`.

```bpl
10-/1 2 3          ⍝ ¯8
10+/2 3⍴⍳6ₓ         ⍝ [13 22]
⊂10 +/ 1 2 3       ⍝ ⊂16
10 20 +/⍤0 1 [2 3]⍴⍳6ₓ ⍝ [13 32]
```

Fixed-width integer reductions keep the promoted fixed type. A wider seed selects a wider accumulator without widening the stored input array:

```bpl
v←[200 100]ₓ₁
+/v                 ⍝ 44ₓ₁
+/vₓ                ⍝ 300ₓ
0ₓ₈+/v              ⍝ 300ₓ₈
(+/)ₓ₈ v            ⍝ 44ₓ₈
```

For an ordinary exact total, use [`+/vₓ`](../numbers.qmd#fixed-width-integers). The fixed-i64 seed makes each addition i64. The seed participates in promotion and cannot narrow wider input. Write `0ₓ₈+/v` or `0ₓ₈ +/ v`, not `0ₓ₈ +/v`. A result suffix converts the completed total and cannot recover wrapped values.

Nested paths use seeded Pick reduction.

```bpl
tree←[[10 20] [30 [40 50]]]
tree⊃/⌽1 1 0       ⍝ 40
```

Use [full windows](up-down-arrow.qmd) for moving reductions.

```bpl
+/↕1 2 3 4         ⍝ 3 5 7
-/⌽↕1 2 3          ⍝ 1 1
+/0↕1 2            ⍝ 0 0 0
```

`f/⍠K` selects the axis. [`⌿`](slash-bar.qmd) defaults to the first.

Several axes form one reduction cell. `f/⍠A Y` ravels each selected cell before reducing, equivalent to `(f/,)¨⊂⍠A Y`. This is an exception to the general rule in [Axis](quad-colon.qmd). A single axis retains ordinary reduction behavior.

```bpl
n←2 2 3⍴⍳6ₓ
+/⍠1 2 n             ⍝ [15 15]ₓ
+/⍠0 2 n             ⍝ [6 24]ₓ
```

Axis order determines the ravel order. Unselected axes retain their order and keys. Selecting every axis gives the reduced value itself, as a dfn along the same axes does.

```bpl
-/⍠0 1 (2 2⍴⍳4ₓ)      ⍝ ¯2ₓ
-/⍠1 0 (2 2⍴⍳4ₓ)      ⍝ ¯4ₓ
```

An empty axis vector makes singleton cells. A seed is passed whole to each cell.

```bpl
+/⍠⍬ [1 2 3]          ⍝ 1 2 3
10+/⍠1 2 (2 2 3⍴⍳6ₓ)   ⍝ [25 25]
```

Float sum and product reductions can reassociate their operands. Other reductions keep operand order.

## Errors

- `RANK`: higher-rank axis specification
- `DOMAIN`: axis vector with repeated or invalid axes, or a subject operand. Replicate with [`#`](hash.qmd)
